rationale: Neither candidate surfaces the ground-truth concern (trust_remote_code kwarg incompatible with locked kernels<0.15.0 installs) since the visible diff doesn't contain that kwarg, so recall is low and roughly equal for both. X digs deeper into the actual core change (the new process-global cache/lock/fallback loop), correctly identifies it has zero direct unit-test coverage, and gives a concrete test-writing recipe plus a cache-reset suggestion — all grounded in specific file/line evidence. Y is well-calibrated and honest (correctly notes failures aren't cached, catches a real but minor lock-scope-across-repos issue) but is less thorough, waving off the test-coverage gap it itself observed rather than flagging it as actionable.
